charts.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow vs Net Income

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total net sales plus royalty and other operating income, in EUR millions.

For UCB: revenue nearly doubled from EUR 3,876m (FY2015) to EUR 7,741m (FY2025), but the path was not smooth -- growth stalled and reversed in FY2022-23 as Vimpat lost U.S. patent exclusivity (2022) and legacy epilepsy brands (Keppra, Vimpat) eroded faster than new launches could offset. FY2024-25 shows a sharp inflection: Bimzelx (bimekizumab, launched 2023) scaled to EUR 2,227m of FY2025 net sales from a standing start, and together with Rystiggo, Zilbrysq, Fintepla and the Evenity profit-share (the 'growth drivers') went from 39% of net sales in H1-2025 to 54% in H1-2026.

What to watch:

  • Whether Bimzelx keeps taking IL-17 new-patient share against Cosentyx, Taltz and the larger IL-23 franchises (Skyrizi, Tremfya)
  • The pace of Cimzia and Briviact loss-of-exclusivity erosion (Briviact lost U.S. exclusivity Feb-2026, EU to follow Aug-2026)
  • Whether growth-driver momentum continues once Bimzelx anniversaries its early launch comps

margins.title: Gross Margin vs Adjusted EBITDA Margin
margins.content:
Gross margin is GrossProfit / Revenue. Adjusted EBITDA margin is UCB's Adjusted (Recurring) EBITDA divided by revenue.

For UCB: UCB publishes no IFRS EBITDA -- the EBITDA figure charted here is UCB's own Adjusted/Recurring EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure the company defines and reconciles itself, not a derivation from reported operating income plus D&A. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from roughly 24% in the mid-2010s to 34% in FY2025 and 40.7% in H1-2026, driven by the mix shift toward higher-margin biologics (Bimzelx, Rystiggo, Zilbrysq) and operating leverage as legacy small-molecule epilepsy revenue (lower R&D and commercial intensity per euro of sales, but also lower price) shrinks as a share of the total.

What to watch:

  • Whether 40.7% (H1-2026) is durable or a cycle peak -- the DCF's own bear case assumes it fades to 27% by FY2035 as Cimzia biosimilars and MFN pricing land
  • Gross margin has been comparatively stable (67-78% across the period) -- most of the margin story is below the gross-profit line, in R&D and SG&A leverage

operatingIncome.title: Operating Income & Net Income
operatingIncome.content:
Reported IFRS operating income and net income, in EUR millions.

For UCB: both lines show the same FY2022-23 dip (Vimpat LOE, rising R&D for the growth-driver pipeline) and FY2024-25 recovery as reported figures, unlike the Adjusted EBITDA series, are not add-back-adjusted -- they carry the full cost of restructuring, in-process R&D charges and one-off items.

What to watch:

  • The gap between operating income growth and revenue growth as a read on operating leverage
  • One-off items (litigation, impairments, M&A costs) that can swing reported net income independently of the underlying business -- FY2026 will carry Candid and Neurona acquisition costs

eps.title: Earnings per Share
eps.content:
Diluted EPS, EUR per share, as reported.

For UCB: EPS tracks net income closely since the share count has been broadly flat (~188-191m shares) across the whole period -- UCB funds a modest buyback (EUR 121m FY2025, EUR 127m H1-2026) that roughly offsets share-based compensation dilution rather than shrinking the count materially. EPS more than doubled from FY2024 (EUR 5.61) to the H1-2026 run-rate.

What to watch:

  • Reported EPS is not the same as UCB's own Core EPS (non-GAAP, excludes amortization of intangibles and one-offs) -- the two can diverge meaningfully in acquisition years

fcf.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow vs Net Income
fcf.content:
Operating cash flow and free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex) as reported, alongside net income for reference.

For UCB: H1-2026 free cash flow is EUR -77m despite operating cash flow of a positive EUR 369m and net income of EUR 1,111m. The swing is a EUR -623m working-capital outflow (receivables and inventory building behind 22% revenue growth, plus EUR -61m of working capital taken on with recent acquisitions) and a capex step-up to EUR 446m for the half -- versus EUR 449m for all of FY2025 -- reflecting the Georgia biologics manufacturing campus build. This is a growth-and-capex-timing effect, not operating deterioration: the DCF explicitly does not treat H1-2026 FCF as the run-rate.

What to watch:

  • Whether the working-capital outflow reverses (receivables collection) or becomes structural as the growth drivers keep scaling
  • Capex normalizing back down once the Georgia campus build completes

capex.title: Capital Expenditure
capex.content:
Cash capital expenditure, EUR millions.

For UCB: capex stepped up sharply to EUR 446m in H1-2026 alone (versus EUR 449m for all of FY2025) on the Georgia biologics manufacturing campus, needed to supply Bimzelx and the growth-driver portfolio at scale. The DCF models capex starting at 8.0% of revenue in FY2026 (versus 5.8% in FY2025) before tapering to 5.5% as the build completes.

What to watch:

  • Capex intensity normalizing once the manufacturing build-out finishes

netDebt.title: Total Debt vs Cash & Equivalents
netDebt.content:
Total interest-bearing debt (bonds, bank borrowings, debentures, lease liabilities) and cash & equivalents, EUR millions.

For UCB: UCB reached a near-net-cash position at FY2025 (net debt EUR -7m), then net debt jumped to EUR 2,821m at H1-2026 (0.8x adjusted EBITDA) after the Candid (USD 2.2bn) and Neurona (USD 1.15bn) acquisitions closed in June 2026 -- both funded with debt. The DCF anchors net debt to this H1-2026 balance sheet, not the stronger FY2025 position, because the acquisitions are the current state of the company.

What to watch:

  • Deleveraging pace given UCB's now-larger cash-generation capacity
  • Whether Candid and Neurona (both pipeline/early-stage assets) deliver revenue to justify the debt taken on

equity.title: Shareholders' Equity
equity.content:
Total shareholders' equity, EUR millions, FY-end only (equity is a stock/balance measure, not additive across interim halves).

For UCB: equity nearly doubled from EUR 5,546m (FY2015) to EUR 10,867m (FY2025) as retained earnings compounded despite a steady dividend, a sign the growth-driver transition has been funded largely from internal cash generation rather than repeated equity issuance.

What to watch:

  • Whether the debt-funded Candid/Neurona acquisitions pressure the equity/debt mix going forward

sbc.title: Stock-Based Compensation & Dividend per Share
sbc.content:
Annual share-based compensation expense and dividend per share, both FY-only (UCB does not disclose an H1 SBC split).

For UCB: SBC is a modest EUR 188m in FY2025, about 2.4% of revenue -- a narrow dilution drag by the standards of this dataset, which is why the DCF's house/street valuation band is comparatively tight (EUR 201.33 vs EUR 221.66, ~10% of the price). The dividend has grown steadily alongside earnings (EUR 3.25/share FY2015 disclosed via DividendPerShare data where available) while remaining well covered by net income.

What to watch:

  • SBC as a share of revenue creeping up as UCB competes for talent against larger U.S. biopharma peers

shares.title: Shares Outstanding
shares.content:
Shares outstanding, millions, FY-end only.

For UCB: the share count has been essentially flat, around 188-191m shares, for the entire FY2015-H1-2026 period -- buybacks (EUR 121m FY2025, EUR 127m H1-2026) broadly offset SBC-driven issuance. The DCF holds the fully diluted count flat at 193.95m for the same reason: SBC is fully expensed in the cash flows, so compounding the share count as well would double-charge the same cost.

What to watch:

  • Whether buyback pace slows now that debt has risen post-Candid/Neurona
